chunks: Verily, Allah, Glory be to Him, sent Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family),

when none among the Arabs read a book or claimed prophethood. He guided the people until he settled them in their place and brought them to their salvation. So their spears (officers) became straight and their conditions settled down.

key_terms.بَوَّأَهُمْ: he settled them / assigned them their place
key_terms.قَنَاتُهُمْ: their spears / their officers (metaphor for leadership structure)

ai.seo_question: What was the condition of the Arabs before Prophet Muhammad's mission according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Sharif al-Radi presents this passage as a rhetorical justification for Imam Ali’s (AS) leadership by contrasting the chaotic, pre-Islamic state of the Arabs with the divine order established through the Prophet. The text emphasizes that the Prophet’s mission was not merely spiritual but also socio-political, transforming a fragmented society into a cohesive community with clear 'channels' of guidance and settled social structures. This historical context underscores the legitimacy of the Ahl al-Bayt’s authority as the inheritors of this divinely ordained stability.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Verily, Allāh sent Muḥammad (S) when none among the Arabs read a book or claimed prophethood.
He guided the people till he took them to their (correct) position and their salvation. So their spears (i.e. officers) became straight and their conditions settled down.
